key_insight: Integrating agentic web-style search into visual perception lets models resolve external, time-sensitive, or long-tail referents before attempting pixel-level localization, enabling correct identification and grounding of objects that are not directly recognizable from image content or frozen model knowledge.
problem_solved: Addresses open-world scenarios where the decisive evidence for identifying a visible object requires querying external facts, recent events, long-tail entities, or multi-hop relations prior to localization.
method: Formalize the challenge as "Perception Deep Research" and define an evaluation setup where perception depends on external information resolution.
Agentic search pipeline: an agent issues targeted web/knowledge queries (multi-hop when needed) to resolve the referent or retrieve disambiguating facts.
Grounding and verification: map the resolved entity/facts to visual candidates using a vision-language grounding module and iteratively verify/ refine localization.
impact: This approach expands visual perception beyond static image cues and model priors, making vision systems robust to real-world, time-sensitive, and long-tail referents—beneficial for tasks like VQA, robotics, and surveillance that need up-to-date or world-aware grounding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agentic search → knowledge retrieval → grounding module → pixel-level localization (with iteration loop)

paper_title: From Web to Pixels: Bringing Agentic Search into Visual Perception
